To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a graph database that provides efficient access to complex pathway knowledge.

the graph database and its Cypher query language provide an efficient access to complex Reactome data, reducing the average time of queries by 93% and providing programmatic access to the Reactome data by a new ContentService (API) that allows object oriented queries as well as more complex queries taking advantage of the underlying graph-based data structure.

we have developed a novel approach to storing Reactome data in a graph-based NoSQL database, Neo4j, and we have developed a new RESTful web service that provides access to the Reactome data stored in the graph database.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the efficient storage and retrieval of biological pathway data.
the development of a novel pathway data resource that is both highly efficient and easy to use.
the development of new technologies and tools for efficient and easy access to complex pathway knowledgebases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Reactome graph database is a high performance data storage for biological pathway data.
graph databases are an ideal solution for storing, querying, and analyzing biological data.
graph databases provide an efficient and effective means to access and query complex biological pathway data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
graph databases provide an efficient way to store and query complex pathway data.
the Reactome graph database and the new ContentService provides an easy to use, high performance and scalable pathway data resource.
the graph database technology provides a more flexible data model, which can be used to represent complex data, such as biological pathways, in a more efficient manner.

a graph database provides an efficient way to access highly interconnected data.
graph databases are a viable solution to store, query and access complex biological data.
the use of graph databases can greatly improve query efficiency for complex data types such as biological pathways.
